summary: Draft Session Manager Kernel record. `TimerCheckFlags` sits under `HKLM\\SYSTEM\\CurrentControlSet\\Control\\Session Manager\\Kernel`, has an explicit repo-doc default of `1`, is absent on the observed clean baseline, produced an exact current-build Unicode string hit in `ntoskrnl.exe`, and has WRK-backed source-enrichment evidence that `KeTimerCheckFlags` is initialized from `KE_TIMER_CHECK_FREES` and later bit-tested in timer code. The broad lightweight runtime batch then wrote the candidate value as `1` and still returned `no-hit`. setting.name: Timer Check Flags
setting.casual_explanation: This appears to be a kernel-level Session Manager setting tied to timer-check behavior. It is kernel-adjacent and is being tracked as a research candidate, not a user-facing tweak.
setting.why_people_change_it: Kernel researchers may inspect this value when investigating timer bookkeeping, timer-free validation behavior, or undocumented kernel timer diagnostics.
setting.tradeoffs_overview: The value has a stronger than usual docs-first evidence chain because it has repo docs, baseline state, exact current-build string presence, WRK semantic source hits, a real write-and-reboot runtime lane, and now dedicated live current-build KD state. It is still too weak for a published tweak because the exact current-build reader path and exact runtime registry read remain unresolved.
setting.professional_notes: Repo docs assign `TimerCheckFlags = 1` under `Session Manager\\Kernel` and map it to `KeTimerCheckFlags`. The observed clean baseline later confirmed that the parent key exists while the value itself is absent. The broad current-build string batch found an exact Unicode hit for `TimerCheckFlags` in `ntoskrnl.exe`. Later source-enrichment over the WRK cache added stronger semantic support than a raw string hit: it retained `extern ULONG KeTimerCheckFlags;`, `ULONG KeTimerCheckFlags = KE_TIMER_CHECK_FREES;`, and a timer-object branch `if ((KeTimerCheckFlags & KE_TIMER_CHECK_FREES) == 0) {`, which strongly suggests the repo-doc default of `1` corresponds to the timer-free check bit being enabled in older kernel source. A later tools-hardened lightweight runtime lane wrote all 21 `Session Manager\\Kernel` batch values, including `TimerCheckFlags = 1`, rebooted once, preserved shell health, and still returned `no-hit` for this specific candidate in the ETW-derived query surface. A dedicated KVM local-KD follow-up then resolved `nt!KeTimerCheckFlags` and directly read its live current-build value as `1`, which aligns with both the repo-doc default and the older WRK initializer. The next proof step is no longer symbol existence or live state; it is a current-build reader or seeding path that explains whether the registry value is still an active override on modern builds.
